title: npm and package.json
idea: npm is Node's package manager: it downloads other people's packages into `node_modules` and records what your project needs in `package.json`.

analogy.text: A shopping list and a pantry: `package.json` is the list, `node_modules` is the pantry, and npm does the shopping.
analogy.breaks: Unlike a list, `package.json` accepts a range of versions, not one exact item.

points: A package is reusable code shared through the npm registry, an online catalogue.
`npm install name` adds one package; plain `npm install` installs everything `package.json` lists.
`package-lock.json` pins the exact versions installed, so every machine gets the same code.
`npm run name` runs a `scripts` entry; `npm start` and `npm test` are shortcuts.

messages.label: npm install dotenv
messages.note: You ask npm for a package by name, from a terminal inside your project folder.

messages.label: find dotenv
messages.note: npm asks the public registry for a matching version of `dotenv`, plus anything it depends on.

messages.label: package files
messages.note: The registry sends back the files for the chosen versions.

messages.label: node_modules/
messages.note: npm unpacks the code into the `node_modules` folder.

messages.label: package.json
messages.note: npm adds `dotenv` under `dependencies`, the list of packages the project needs.

messages.label: package-lock.json
messages.note: npm writes the exact versions it installed into `package-lock.json`.

code.title: Commands
code.caption: A first session in a new project folder.

walk.text: Create a starter `package.json`, answering every question with its default.
Download `dotenv` into `node_modules` and add it to `dependencies`.
`--save-dev` lists a tool under `devDependencies`: needed while developing, not in production.
Run the `dev` script. You add scripts by editing `package.json`; custom names need `npm run`.
With no name, `npm install` installs what `package.json` lists, at the versions in `package-lock.json`.

code.title: The manifest
code.caption: What `package.json` can look like after those commands.

walk.text: Name and version identify your project.
`type: module` makes `.js` files ES modules; without it they are CommonJS.
`scripts` names commands that you run with `npm run`.
`dependencies` lists what the app needs at run time. Chapter 4 explains the `^`.
`devDependencies` lists tools needed only while you develop.

code.title: Using the package
code.caption: A name without `./` is a package, so Node looks in `node_modules`. dotenv turns `KEY=value` text into an object of strings.

pitfalls: Keep `node_modules` out of git with a `.gitignore` entry; `npm install` rebuilds it.
Commit `package-lock.json`, so teammates and servers install the same versions.
Check a package's exact name before installing; look-alike names exist to trick you.

quiz.q: A teammate clones your project (without `node_modules`) and runs `node app.mjs`. What happens?
options: Node downloads `dotenv` on the first run
quiz.why: `node_modules` is not in git, and Node never downloads packages. Run `npm install` first; it reads `package.json` and the lockfile.

takeaway: `package.json` lists what you need; `npm install` makes it so.
